$doc: Vyomi capability registry — API Gateway (apigateway.googleapis.com v1). See kms.json for the contract.

gcp.apigateway.apis-configs-gateways.title: API Gateway API (apis, API configs from OpenAPI 2.0, gateways)
limitations: Real control plane: API configs are validated like the real service (swagger 2.0, info.title, paths, an operationId and an https x-google-backend address per operation, duplicate operationIds, base64 document contents), a config served by a gateway can't be deleted, an API with configs can't be deleted, gateways must point at an existing config and get a {id}-{hash}.{region code}.gateway.dev hostname. Every mutation is a long-running operation that is already done.

Real data plane on the shared gateway engine (core/gcp_apigateway_gateway.py over core/apigatewayv2_gateway.py; throttle/quota counters, JWT + RS256/JWKS verification, hop-header stripping and backend URL building come from core/gateway_common.py, shared with AWS API Gateway v1/v2 and Azure APIM; RS256 proven against a real keypair and a served JWKS in test_gateway_rs256_jwks.py): a request to https://{id}-{hash}.{code}.gateway.dev/... (or the simulator origin's /gcpgw/{gatewayId}/...) is routed by the config's paths and forwarded to the operation's x-google-backend address (CONSTANT_ADDRESS / APPEND_PATH_TO_ADDRESS) with real HTTP. apiKey security is enforced against API Keys created through the API Keys v2 API (400 invalid key / 401 missing key), oauth2/JWT security checks iss, aud (x-google-audiences), exp/nbf and the RS256 signature against x-google-jwks_uri (fails closed when no verifier or no cryptography is available), and x-google-quota metricCosts are enforced against x-google-management quota limits (fixed 1-second / 1-minute windows per project, 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED).

Nano (browser tab) has no sockets, so the engine splits the call (plan() = route/auth/quota, counted once; finish() = response) and awaits a JS bridge (wasm/gw-bridge.js) that POSTs the backend call to your local `vyomi-tunnel` /gw-egress. The relay forwards ONLY backends you mapped with `vyomi-tunnel gateway-backend <https origin>=<local origin>` (anything else 502; metadata/link-local refused, redirects never followed, size/time/method limits, per-session rate limit, every call logged; needs your signed-in tunnel and the Nano page origin). Without a local tunnel, public https backends on an allow-list (run.app, cloudfunctions.net, azurewebsites.net, execute-api, ...) go through the hosted relay (443 only, no IPs, 1 MiB / 4 MiB / 15 s, needs a registered Nano session). Otherwise the call answers 503 UNAVAILABLE naming the fix. Chrome asks once to allow the page to reach 127.0.0.1. Verified in Python and node; the browser path is covered by the Nano e2e noted in docs/architecture/v4.0/GATEWAY-NANO-FORWARDING.md. AWS API Gateway v1/v2 and Azure APIM use the same bridge (resumable engine run, see their capability files). Not modelled: Service Management / Service Control activation, per-user quota dimensions, ESPv2 JWT claim-to-header, Firebase auth, CORS config (the backend answers OPTIONS), request/response transformation, gRPC, and real *.gateway.dev DNS/TLS (use the Host header or /gcpgw/).

Known limit (v4.0.0 beta): on Nano a RS256/JWKS (oauth2) token cannot be verified yet, so a route secured by a JWT answers 401 (fails closed) even for a valid token; API-key security, quota and forwarding work. Use the offline appliance or Mesh to exercise JWT auth.
